The selected snapshot retains literal source-listed contractor names within the Clermont capture. Counts of named permit rows, distinct source strings and associated properties have different grains; consult coverage:clermont-contractors for the exact selected coverage counts. This is partial coverage, not countywide or reconciled legal-company identity.
Selected retained Clermont permit rows: 58,495. Catalog implementation/certification labels do not erase previously acquired rows.
A missing captured name remains unknown/not established. Legacy tokens contractor_absent_on_permit and contractor_gated_403 are capture diagnostics, not established absence, owner-builder proof or verified identity. Neither absence nor licensing may be inferred from an owner name.
Retained historical source observations are loaded, not accepted current-open status, open duration, roofing classification, completion, or verified legal-company/license identity. These conclusions remain unknown, not zero or false.
For unincorporated Lake County, the route to contractor names is a Chapter 119 records request to the Lake County Office of Building Services for the complete CD Plus permit history including contractor of record.

chunks.title: Clermont — permit jurisdiction in Lake County, Florida
chunks.text:
Clermont — permit jurisdiction in Lake County, Florida

Catalog source: pipeline/docs/lake-sources.yaml (repository path; authority for catalogued access states, permit systems and records-request recipients/routes). Selected-row counts and capability limits are bound separately to the cited coverage artifact.
Selected run 20260916T181000Z retains 58,495 Clermont permit rows in permit-table.parquet. Acquisition is established independently of the catalog's acceptance/certification state. The source catalog records this portal as OPEN and machine-readable. An open portal alone proves neither acquisition nor accepted current status. Retained historical source observations are loaded, not accepted current-open status, open duration, roofing classification, completion, or verified legal-company/license identity. These conclusions remain unknown, not zero or false.
Retained capture window: 2015–2026; all required portal-year partitions captured: true. This is not proof of complete predecessor/archive history or today's permit status.
Permit system vendor: CentralSquare eTRAKiT 3.
Permit portal: https://etrakit.clermontfl.org/eTRAKiT3/Search/permit.aspx (historical-search).
Catalog historical-record flag: true. Catalog anonymous-access flag: true. These flags are not an exhaustive statement about held records or loaded selected-run rows.
Catalog acquisition/acceptance state: certified; enumeration status certified-enumerated; adapter etrakit. These catalog labels do not negate retained selected-run rows.
Parcel search: SITE_APN search labelled "AK NUMBER", which is the NAL ALT_KEY.
Measured throughput: Benchmarked 2026-09-11 at concurrency 1 and 2, sixty-three requests in total, zero failures. Session bootstrap p50 759 ms and yields a 5,035-entry registered-contractor directory. Parcel search by SITE_APN p50 624 ms, returning a parcel's whole permit history in one response - 8.2 permits per permitted parcel across the ten sampled. Prefix list search p50 672 ms, 20 rows a page and capped at every depth-2 prefix tried. Detail capture p50 1,077 ms at concurrency 1 (0.91 req/s) and p50 1,145 ms, p95 2,585 ms at concurrency 2 (1.55 req/s), at 854 KB a page. Safe concurrency is 2. Separately measured ceiling: a run of roughly 2,500 detail requests at concurrency 2 over about 80 minutes ended with the host accepting TCP and never answering, while unloaded probes returned HTTP 200 in 2.0 s throughout - load-induced and transient, so the lever is cumulative request rate, not worker count. Estimated full download, at concurrency 2 and the measured failure rate: 0.6 h for one permit year by prefix enumeration, 8 to 9 h and about 50 GB of raw HTML for the whole 15-26 history, and 5.0 h for a parcel-keyed pass over the 50,447 CLERMONT-mailing seed parcels. All three are inside the 48-hour county-ingest-run gate..
Probe result: Re-probed 2026-09-09: the permit search page returns HTTP 200, 785,477 bytes in 1.9 s with no session, no challenge and no login. The parcel field is labelled "AK NUMBER" and posts as SITE_APN, which is the NAL ALT_KEY, so the join needs no translation. Search is an ASP.NET postback carrying __VIEWSTATE, so an adapter must round-trip the form; permit detail is reachable by a plain GET once a permit number is known. Re-probed 2026-09-11 after an outage: HTTP 200 in 2.0 s, unchanged.
Catalog limitation (selected coverage governs retained rows): Detail pages expose contractor names and inspection history, which the county layer does not, and this is the only open route to contractor of record anywhere in Lake County. The September 11 pilot enumerated 4,132 year-26 permits over 2,656 parcels; that pilot is historical, not the completed full harvest. The retained certified baseline now contains 58,495 captured permits across all twelve 2015-2026 partitions, with zero retryable pending and zero proven-dead records. Source detail HTML, normalized records and export digests remain retained. The export contains 9,969 literal ROOF/REROOF records; this is a source permit-type count, not an accepted primary-roof replacement count. Per-record successful capture timestamps were not preserved, so sealing/certification times must not be used as current-status clocks. Routing by mailing city over-selects heavily - 50,447 seed parcels carry a CLERMONT mailing city while the portal knows about 2,656 a year - so the portal's own answer, not the city string, decides membership. The prior year-26 capture classified 71 permits with no parcel key as dead. The repaired full harvester retains each accessible detail and its raw evidence as a valid-unlinked permit; only a genuine permanent source failure is recorded as dead.

chunks.title: Permit jurisdictions in Lake County, Florida — who issues permits and which ones are blocked
chunks.text:
Permit jurisdictions in Lake County, Florida — who issues permits and which ones are blocked

Catalog source: pipeline/docs/lake-sources.yaml (repository path; authority for catalogued access states, permit systems and records-request recipients/routes). Selected-row counts and capability limits are bound separately to the cited coverage artifact.
Lake County permitting is not a single countywide system. There are 15 permit-issuing jurisdictions: unincorporated Lake County plus 14 independent municipalities, each running its own building department and its own permit software.
The selected coverage receipt establishes retained permit rows from 2 jurisdictions: Unincorporated Lake County (Perconti CD Plus county layer), Clermont (CentralSquare eTRAKiT portal). Retained acquisition is separate from accepted/certified lifecycle evidence.
Jurisdictions not listed in the selected run's complete source counts: Groveland (catalog access blocked, blocked-login-required); Eustis (catalog access blocked, blocked-bot-challenge); Minneola (catalog access blocked, blocked-cloudflare-challenge); Leesburg (catalog access blocked, blocked-captcha); Tavares (catalog access unavailable, unreachable-from-egress); Mount Dora (catalog access blocked, blocked-bot-challenge); Umatilla (catalog access manual-only, no-public-historical-search); Astatula (catalog access manual-only, no-public-historical-search); Fruitland Park (catalog access blocked, blocked-bot-challenge); Howey-in-the-Hills (catalog access blocked, blocked-captcha); Lady Lake (catalog access blocked, blocked-egress-tls-failure); Mascotte (catalog access blocked, blocked-captcha); Montverde (catalog access manual-only, no-public-historical-search).
Retained historical source observations are loaded, not accepted current-open status, open duration, roofing classification, completion, or verified legal-company/license identity. These conclusions remain unknown, not zero or false.
Every blocked jurisdiction has a named public-records request recipient in the source catalog, so the records can still be obtained by a Chapter 119 request. Ask for the jurisdiction by name to get its recipient office, request channel and system scope.
Historical source-catalog finding, not a new selected-run measurement: The county CD Plus layer is NOT a countywide permit archive. Two measured limits. First, jurisdiction: a spatial test of every permit parcel against the 14 Census city polygons puts 45 of 17,915 features (0.25%) inside any city limit, and those are Lake County government facilities that the county permits for itself. The layer is unincorporated Lake County only, and no municipality delegates permitting to the county. Mailing city is not a jurisdiction signal - 4,688 features carry a CLERMONT mailing address while sitting in unincorporated south Lake. Second, time: Permit_LastModDate spans 2025-09-09 to 2026-09-08, exactly a 365-day rolling window, and only 846 of 17,671 permits (4.8%) were issued before 2024-09-09. The layer publishes recently-modified permits, not history.
Catalogued roofing type tokens: RF, RFC, RFR, ROC, ROR; open-status tokens: APPLY, INSPECT, ISSUED, READY, RENEWED. Tokens alone do not establish accepted roofing or current-open conclusions in the selected run.
